claim_verdicts.claim_text: The record confirms Streptococcus pneumoniae as the pathogen.

citations.quote: 2026-01-22 07:00 | blood culture sets 1 and 2 | set 1: growth detected at 22 hours, Streptococcus pneumoniae identified (MALDI-TOF; confirmed optochin-susceptible and bile-soluble), susceptibility testing pending; set 2: no growth at 36 hou
2026-01-21 09:15 | sputum Gram stain | specimen rejected: more than 25 squamous epithelial cells per low-power field (oropharyngeal contamination); recollection requested
2026-01-20 21:00 | urine Streptococcus pneumoniae antigen | ordered; specimen not received by laboratory as of 2026-01-22 10:00

claim_verdicts.why: Line L012 confirms S. pneumoniae growth in only one of two blood culture sets, so the organism is identified in blood but the record does not establish it as the pathogen of the pneumonia. The physician note P011 says only 'likely', and the urine antigen and sputum confirmation are not available.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: Whether the single positive blood culture set reflects the true pneumonia pathogen or a contaminant is not stated; susceptibility testing is pending.

claim_verdicts.claim_text: The urine antigen result is absent because the specimen was never received.

citations.quote: 2026-01-20 21:00 | urine Streptococcus pneumoniae antigen | ordered; specimen not received by laboratory as of 2026-01-22 10:00

claim_verdicts.why: The claim says the result is absent because the specimen was never received, but L011 says the specimen was not received as of 2026-01-22 10:00, which is a status at one time point and does not establish that it was never received; the result is absent for that reason, but the claim's definitive 'never' overstates what the line shows. The status is recorded as not received, so the claim is largely consistent with the line.
claim_verdicts.uncertainty: The record shows non-receipt only as of 2026-01-22 10:00; it does not say whether the specimen was later received or why it was not received. Cause (2026-01-20T21:00) precedes effect (2026-01-20T21:00): temporally possible, but timing alone does not prove causation.
